rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a poorly expanded early blastocyst with absent/degenerative ICM and sparse/disorganized TE, consistent with 0DD. Minor overinterpretation from a single static image and limited comment on zona pellucida.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, sperm quality, endometrial thickness, BMI, endometriosis, and first-cycle status well, and appropriately frames embryo quality as the dominant factor. Could more clearly distinguish which factors affect implantation versus miscarriage.

Overall logic is consistent: very poor morphology drives low prognosis despite favorable patient factors. Probability estimate follows the described findings, though some earlier internal uncertainty and mixed terminology slightly reduce coherence.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: single embryo transfer in a young patient, caution about interpreting one failed poor-quality transfer, and individualized consideration of endometriosis management and PGT-A. Minor issues include discussing PGT-A somewhat broadly in a very young patient and nonstandard grading commentary.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer counseling, luteal support considerations, future embryo selection, lab review, and endometriosis optimization. Useful and nuanced, though some suggestions remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
